findings.title: OAuth helper imports decodeOAuthState from a path that does not exist
findings.body: After the move into _utils/oauth, createOAuthAppCredential imports decodeOAuthState from "../oauth/decodeOAuthState". That resolves to _utils/oauth/oauth/decodeOAuthState, which is not a file. The module is in the same directory (./decodeOAuthState). Every callback that creates credentials through this helper (HubSpot, Salesforce, Stripe, Zoom, MS Teams, Zoho, Webex, Tandem, and others) will fail to load, so those OAuth installs cannot complete.

findings.title: Google refresh persists the Zod result object instead of the tokens
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a SafeParseResult ({ success, data }), not the credential payload. Google Calendar assigns that object to key and writes it with prisma.credential.update. On every access-token refresh the stored credential is replaced by { success, data }, dropping access_token, refresh_token, and expiry_date. Subsequent Google Calendar and Meet calls then fail schema parse or auth.

findings.title: Sync-mode token schema cannot accept a real token response
findings.body: minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()], which are the literal property names "ZodString" and "ZodOptional", not a catchall. Zod object schemas also strip unknown keys. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, safeParse requires a numeric "ZodString" field and rejects normal { access_token, expires_in } bodies, so every synced refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". The same function then, if refresh_token is absent, writes the literal string "refresh_token" onto the parsed data (line 26), which callers persist and use for the next refresh, permanently invalidating the grant.

findings.title: Sync refresh returns an unparsed, unauthenticated fetch Response
findings.body: When credential sync is on, refreshOAuthTokens POSTs only calcomUserId and appSlug as form fields and returns the raw fetch Response. There is no shared secret or other authenticator, so the parent app cannot tell this call from an anonymous request, and Cal.com will treat whatever body comes back as tokens. Callers are also not updated for this shape: Google reads res.data, HubSpot treats the return value as a HubspotToken, and Zoho Bigin/CRM read axios .data. Those paths throw or store undefined tokens whenever sync is enabled. The Zoom caller also passes app slug "zoomvideo" while credentials are stored as appId "zoom", so a sync lookup by slug will miss the app.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin refresh sends credential id as the Cal user id
findings.body: refreshAccessToken calls refreshOAuthTokens(..., credentialId), but credentialId is credential.id, not credential.userId. The sync endpoint therefore receives the credential primary key as calcomUserId and will mint or look up tokens for the wrong user (or none). Bigin token refresh is wrong for every synced user.

findings.title: Salesforce refresh uses prisma without importing it and keeps the old access token
findings.body: getClient now calls prisma.credential.update, but this file never imports prisma, so loading SalesforceCalendarService throws ReferenceError and every Salesforce booking fails. Even if prisma were imported, the jsforce Connection is still constructed with credentialKey.access_token (the pre-refresh token) and credentialKey.instance_url, while the newly parsed access token is only written to the database. API calls would keep using the expired token. parseRefreshTokenResponse also throws on failure, so the following !accessTokenParsed.success branch is dead.

findings.title: Credential webhook accepts any method and writes unvalidated decrypted JSON
findings.body: The handler never checks req.method, and appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse is not caught, so a bad body becomes an unhandled 500. After a successful secret check it JSON.parses the decrypted string and writes that value straight into credential.key (create or update) with no schema for the app. A sync sender bug, or anyone who has the webhook secret, can replace a user's OAuth credential with arbitrary JSON. findFirst-then-create is also not transactional, so concurrent deliveries can insert duplicate credentials for the same user and app, and later findFirst updates will only touch one of them.
